note: Original description (as Eutermes rotundiceps), with the alate, the queen, the soldier and the worker all present. The genus name was later separated off as Rotunditermes by Holmgren. The text was extracted by OCR from a library scan on the Internet Archive; the original is in German, and the segment counts misread by the OCR (lögliedrig/13gliedrig) have been corrected from the context.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Placed in the genus Eutermes in the original.) Total length with wings 16 mm; body length without wings 8 mm; head length 1.26 mm, head width 1.3 mm; forewing length 14 mm, hindwing length 13 mm. The upper surfaces of the head and pronotum are brown, the meso- and metanotal tergites light rusty brown, the sternites concolorous, the legs rusty yellow. The head, thorax and the marginal vein of the wing bear fairly dense long hairs; the wing is densely covered with short hairs; the sternites are densely hairy. The head is about as long as wide, narrowing anteriorly into a triangle, the posterior margin rounded; the frons has a groove, with a distinct fontanelle and a fine transverse groove; the ocellus is fairly close to the compound eye, large, oblique, oval; on each side before the fontanelle there are 2 small round pale spots, and on each side before the ocellus 1 large transversely placed oval pale spot; the posterior margin of the base of the grooved middle part of the postclypeus is angled, its anterior margin straight; the tip is narrow, the lateral corners and the middle part slightly elongate; the labrum is lingulate; the mandible has 3 teeth before the basal tooth; the antenna has 16 segments, segment 2 about twice the size of segment 3, segment 4 larger than segment 3 and round. The pronotum is flat, the anterior margin slightly concave, the lateral corners rounded, the posterior margin arcuate, about twice as wide as long, with a fine median line. The wings are brownish black; the media of the forewing is usually simple, the submedia has 12—13 branches, of which the inner 6 are thickened; the media of the hindwing is simple, the submedia has 12—15 branches, of which the inner 6—7 are thickened.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 3.15—4.5 mm; head length 1.8 mm; head width 1.26 mm; length of the frontal process 0.7 mm. The head is yellow with a few fairly long setae; the frontal process rusty brown; the antenna rusty yellow or rusty brown; the tergites and sternites light rusty yellow; the legs more or less straw-coloured; the thoracic and abdominal segments bear scattered hairs or setae. The head and thorax are held almost at a right angle. Seen from above the head is almost circular, with a weak constriction behind the antennae; the frontal process is of even width, is not a direct prolongation of the head and is fairly clearly demarcated from it. The antenna has 13 segments; segment 3 (composed of 2) is distinctly longer than segments 2 and 4, segment 5 longer than segment 4. The pronotum is saddle-shaped, the anterior margin raised fairly strongly.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body length 4 mm; head length 1.2 mm; head width 0.9 mm. Pale straw-yellow; the head and thorax bear a few setae, the abdomen more hairs. The sides of the head are fairly straight, slightly diverging anteriorly; the widest part is before the antennae, where the sides of the head are strongly flattened and turn abruptly downwards, converging towards the mandibular base; the base of the grooved middle part of the postclypeus is strongly raised; the labrum is lingulate. The right mandible has 2 apical teeth, 1 middle tooth close to the apical teeth (its posterior edge long) and 1 bidentate basal tooth; the left mandible has 2 apical teeth, 1 smaller middle tooth and 1 large, wide, round and sharp basal tooth. The antenna has 14 segments, segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 with a false articulation and so appearing 2-segmented, segment 4 short, segment 5 longer than segment 4. The anterior margin of the pronotum is strongly raised.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The queen has a body length of 18 mm and an abdominal width of 6.5 mm. Closely related to Eutermes arenarius; Holmgren pointed out that the largest of the 3 soldier morphotypes of E. diversimiles Silvestri is similar to E. rotundiceps, and that E. vetox is linked to E. rotundiceps and E. arenarius through E. diversimiles. Locality: Bolivia (Tuiche, Prov. de Caupolican).
